## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Because Bakkula's confession spans eighty years of monastic life, the sutta's internal chronology implies that it was delivered at least thirty-five years after the Buddha's Parinibbāna [Anālayo 2011]. In accord with this, the commentary *Papañcasūdanī* explicitly records that MN 124 was incorporated into the canon only during the second communal recitation (*saṅgīti*) [Anālayo 2011]. Structurally, MN 124 shares with the preceding *Acchariyaabbhuta Sutta* (MN 123) a repetitive refrain formula that records each marvellous quality (*acchariya-abbhuta*) as something kept in mind by reciters, a mnemonic technique suggested to have facilitated the admission and preservation of later additions within the oral transmission [Anālayo 2011].
DharmaNexus aligns MN 124 with MĀ 34 and identifies 319 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 42 canonical texts [DharmaNexus]. Its primary partner is MN 123 (122 matches, 3,969 characters), reflecting their shared refrain formulas, along with substantial doctrinal and phraseological parallels in the *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47), the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), and the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35) [DharmaNexus; Anālayo 2011].
